items.passage: Saga had been folding dumplings wrong for three weeks before she told me about the offer. A hotel kitchen in Seoul wanted her, with a salary I could not match and a uniform with her name stitched on the pocket. I said nothing for a while and kept skimming the broth, which needs skimming whether or not anyone is leaving. When I was her age, I left a stall like this one and came back after a year, ashamed of how little the city had taught me. I did not tell her that. Some lessons spoil when they are handed over. Instead I showed her once more how to pinch the edge so the seam holds in boiling water, and I watched her hands rather than her face. Outside, the wind off the harbor rattled the plastic awning, and a customer called for a second bowl.
items.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward Saga's offer?
options: Open resentment toward Saga for considering a job that would leave the stall short of help
Quiet relief that Saga will soon leave a stall where she has struggled to learn the work
Private unease held in check by a belief that Saga must reach her own decision
Firm certainty that Saga will return once she finds the city has little to teach her
items.explanation: 화자는 제안을 듣고 한동안 말없이 국물만 걷어 내며 감정을 드러내지 않는다. 자신도 젊을 때 떠났다가 부끄럽게 돌아왔다는 경험을 말하지 않고 '어떤 교훈은 건네면 상한다'고 여기는 데서, 걱정은 있지만 Saga가 스스로 결정해야 한다고 믿는 태도가 드러난다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A의 노골적 원망이나 B의 안도는 근거가 없고, D는 화자의 과거 경험을 Saga의 미래에 대한 확신으로 잘못 확대한 것이다.

items.passage: When Amelie arrived at the laundromat on Calle Feria each afternoon, her grandfather Ivan was already scolding the dryers in a language she was only half learning. He had kept the place open for thirty-one years, through two floods and a decade in which the neighbors bought machines of their own. His ledger was a schoolchild's notebook, and its columns had been thinning for years; still he wrote the day's few coins in a careful hand, as if neatness might persuade the numbers. Amelie practiced verbs by reading his labels aloud: wash, wait, return. He corrected her accent with more patience than he ever showed the machines. Neither of them mentioned the letter from the landlord, folded under the coin tray where it had rested for a month. Down the street, a bakery lowered its shutter, and the smell of anise drifted in with the heat.
items.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward Ivan's efforts to keep the laundromat open?
options: Mocking, treating his careful bookkeeping as proof that he misunderstands basic arithmetic
Admiring, presenting his persistence as certain to restore the business to its old success
Indifferent, recording his habits without hinting that the business faces real difficulty
Tender yet realistic, honoring his diligence while noting signs that the business is failing
items.explanation: 서술자는 Ivan이 31년간 가게를 지켜 온 끈기와 정성스러운 장부 기록을 따뜻하게 그린다. 동시에 장부의 줄이 해마다 줄어들고 집주인의 편지가 한 달째 동전 접시 밑에 놓여 있다는 점을 짚어 가게가 기울고 있음을 분명히 한다. 이 두 단서를 함께 보면 D가 정답이다. A의 조롱, B의 낙관적 확신, C의 무관심은 이런 이중적 시선과 맞지 않는다.

items.passage: Film canisters rattled on the shelf when the power died, and I found myself stuck in a projection booth in Lima with a stranger named Sipho, who had come to repair the lens. For two hours we waited for the street to come back on. He told me that in his family a goodbye was never said at the door; you walked the guest to the corner, so the parting happened in open air. I had always considered such rituals a little theatrical. Yet when the lights returned and he packed his tools, I caught myself following him down the narrow stairs, past the ticket window, all the way to the end of the block. I am still not sure whose custom I was honoring. A bus went by with its windows fogged, carrying no one I knew.
items.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward Sipho's custom of parting?
options: Former skepticism that has softened into a reluctant, almost unconscious acceptance
Steady contempt for a custom that the narrator regards as needlessly theatrical
Nostalgic longing for a family tradition the narrator practiced as a young child
Polite curiosity that never affects how the narrator actually behaves toward Sipho
items.explanation: 화자는 처음에 그런 의식을 '다소 연극적'이라고 여겼다고 밝힌다. 그러나 불이 들어오자 자신도 모르게 Sipho를 따라 골목 끝까지 걸어가며, 누구의 관습을 따른 것인지 모르겠다고 말한다. 두 부분을 연결하면 회의가 무의식적인 수용으로 바뀐 A가 정답이다. B는 앞부분만 본 오답이고, C는 지문에 없는 어린 시절을, D는 실제 행동 변화를 무시한다.

items.passage: Aunt Themba never wasted water. Each morning in the community garden off Mirpur Road, she filled one dented can and divided it among the chilies, the gourds, and Edith's struggling mint, giving the mint the least. Edith, who cooked for the stall her aunt ran, assumed this was a judgment on her. That afternoon a neighbor mentioned, as if everyone knew, that Themba had once given up a place at a teachers' college so that Edith's mother could finish school instead. Edith said nothing. Later, watering alone, she noticed that her aunt's own plot, the farthest from the tap, had always received the last and smallest share. A rickshaw bell sounded beyond the fence, and pigeons lifted off the tin roof of the tool shed.
items.question: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
options: To recount how Edith learns that a neighbor knows private details of her family's past
To show Edith beginning to see her aunt's strictness as a pattern of quiet self-denial
To describe the daily routine of tending a crowded community garden in Dhaka
To suggest that every family hides sacrifices its younger members will never learn of
items.explanation: 앞부분에서 Edith는 고모가 자기 민트에 물을 가장 적게 주는 것을 자신에 대한 평가로 받아들인다. 이웃에게서 고모가 동생을 위해 교대 입학을 포기했다는 사실을 들은 뒤, 고모 자신의 밭이 늘 가장 적은 물을 받아 왔다는 점을 알아차린다. 두 근거를 이으면 엄격함을 조용한 자기희생으로 다시 보게 되는 과정이 요지이므로 B가 정답이다. A는 일화만 요약했고, C는 소재만 같으며, D는 지나치게 일반적인 교훈이다.

items.passage: Who pays a tutor in oranges? Miriam had asked this aloud the first week, when Fiorella refused her envelope of coins and accepted only a sack of fruit from the barge's hold. Since then the tutor had come every Thursday, climbing down the ladder with her books wrapped against the river damp, and Miriam's brother had begun reading the cargo lists to the crew with sudden pride. Miriam kept the coins in a tin, telling herself she would insist next time. But this evening she found her brother's old shoes, the pair that had split at the toe, replaced by a sturdy one, with a note in Fiorella's handwriting tucked inside: outgrown by my nephew. Miriam set the tin back on its shelf, unopened. Along the bank, a crane swung a pallet of cement toward a waiting truck.
items.question: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
options: To recount how Miriam's brother improves his reading by studying cargo lists with the crew
To explain why Fiorella prefers to be paid in fruit rather than in coins for her lessons
To trace Miriam's shift from wanting to settle a debt to accepting Fiorella's kindness
To suggest that generosity between strangers always means more than any form of payment
items.explanation: 앞부분에서 Miriam은 동전을 깡통에 모아 두며 다음에는 꼭 값을 치르겠다고 다짐한다. 그러나 Fiorella가 몰래 동생의 새 신발을 놓고 간 것을 발견한 뒤에는 깡통을 열지 않은 채 선반에 되돌려 놓는다. 이 대비에서 빚을 갚으려던 태도가 호의를 받아들이는 태도로 바뀌는 과정이 요지이므로 C가 정답이다. A는 세부 일화만, B는 소재는 같지만 목적이 다르며, D는 지나친 일반화다.

items.passage: Moira and I spent most of one winter competing to sell pastries in the lobby of a cinema in Samarkand that showed films only on weekends. Each Friday I arrived early to claim the table beside the poster of a forgotten comedy, and each Friday she was already there, her trays set out in tight rows. I used to count her customers instead of serving my own. In February the projector broke, and for three weeks no one came at all. We sat on opposite benches, then on the same bench, trading samples out of boredom. I learned that she folded her dough twice where I folded mine four times, and that her version was better. When the films returned, I set up wherever there was space. Snow slid from the marquee in long, soft sheets.
items.question: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
options: To describe the narrator's rivalry with Moira over the best table in the cinema lobby
To explain the differences between two techniques for folding pastry dough
To argue that competition between small businesses usually harms everyone involved
To show how an enforced pause loosened the narrator's habit of rivalry with Moira
items.explanation: 앞부분에서 화자는 매주 좋은 자리를 차지하려 하고 자기 손님 대신 Moira의 손님 수를 셀 만큼 경쟁에 매여 있었다. 영사기가 고장 나 손님이 끊긴 동안 같은 벤치에 앉아 반죽법을 배우고, 영화가 다시 시작되자 아무 자리에나 가판을 차린다. 두 장면의 대비가 습관을 내려놓는 과정을 보여 주므로 D가 정답이다. A는 앞부분 일화만, B는 소재만 같고, C는 지나치게 일반적인 주장이다.

items.passage: When the monsoon filled our cellar in Karachi, my twin, Nadeesha, and I had been dividing our late father's house for two months without once mentioning why he had left it to us in equal halves. We split the furniture by alternating choices, the books by shelf, the kitchen by drawer. Every list was polite and complete, and none of it touched the subject. The flood made lists useless. We waded in together, passing up boxes neither of us had labeled, and in one of them were letters he had written to each of us and never sent. We read them sitting on the stairs, our feet still in the water, and for the first time that year we argued, loudly, about him. By evening the pump had begun its slow work, coughing brown water into the lane.
items.question: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
options: To show how an accident broke the careful silence that had shaped the twins' dealings
To recount the method the twins used to divide their father's furniture and books
To describe the damage that a monsoon flood caused to a family home in Karachi
To suggest that arguments between siblings are a healthy part of every family's grief
items.explanation: 앞부분에서 쌍둥이는 가구와 책을 정중하게 나누면서도 아버지에 관한 핵심 주제는 한 번도 꺼내지 않는다. 홍수로 목록이 쓸모없어지고 부치지 않은 편지를 발견한 뒤, 그해 처음으로 아버지에 대해 크게 다툰다. 두 장면의 대비가 사고로 침묵이 깨지는 과정을 보여 주므로 A가 정답이다. B는 일화만 요약했고, C는 소재는 같지만 목적이 다르며, D는 지나치게 일반적인 교훈이다.

items.passage: Hollis stacked the last chairs in the camp dining hall while Piper counted the day's take from the camp store, which came to less than the cost of the ice cream they had ordered. Their mother had eaten lunch at the corner table by the window every summer for forty years, watching the canoes cross the lake. Even now, on her slow days, she asked each morning to be wheeled to a window. Piper had brought the brochure for the care home in Burlington twice before. This time Hollis took it, read it through, and asked whether any of the rooms faced the water. Piper looked up, surprised; he had expected the usual refusal. Through the screen door came the clatter of the kitchen crew hosing down the trays.
items.question: Based on the text, why does Hollis most likely ask whether the rooms face the water?
options: He hopes to delay the decision by raising questions that Piper cannot answer
He believes the store's finances will improve once their mother has moved
He worries that the care home in Burlington charges more for lakeside rooms
He wants his mother to keep something of the lake view she has long valued
items.explanation: 지문 중간에서 어머니는 40년 동안 창가 자리에서 호수를 바라보았고, 지금도 매일 아침 창가로 데려가 달라고 한다는 점이 제시된다. 이 두 단서를 이으면 Hollis가 방이 물을 향하는지 묻는 이유는 어머니가 아끼던 풍경을 지켜 주고 싶어서임을 알 수 있다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A는 평소의 거부 감정에서, B는 이사의 결과를 동기로 착각한 것이며, C는 지문에 없는 비용 문제를 끌어온 것이다.

items.passage: Rumors travel faster than buses. Xinyi, who had spent thirty years as a judge before retiring to the hills outside Hanoi, knew this better than most. Waiting at the mountain stop, she watched Nguyen, the young clerk from the district office, climb the road with his jaw set. Someone had carried to the landlord's wife what Nguyen had said about the landlord, and now the whole village was repeating it. Xinyi offered him half her bench. She had learned long ago that a story repeated often enough grows teeth, and that once it bites, no ruling can unsay it. She told him to apologize before evening, plainly and without excuses. Below them, mist filled the valley, and the bus horn sounded around the last bend.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “grows teeth” most nearly suggests that a repeated story
options: becomes more amusing to the villagers each time it is told
loses its details until it no longer resembles the original remark
gains the power to cause real harm to the people it concerns
grows so long that listeners eventually stop paying attention
items.explanation: 이야기가 이빨을 갖게 되면 '한번 물면 어떤 판결로도 되돌릴 수 없다'는 뒤 구절이 이 비유의 의미를 분명히 한다. 또한 Xinyi가 저녁이 되기 전에 사과하라고 서두르게 하는 데서 소문이 실제 해를 끼칠 수 있다는 위기감이 드러난다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A의 재미, B의 왜곡, D의 지루함은 '문다'는 이미지와 맞지 않는다.

items.passage: Years later, Irena would still remember the kettle shrieking while she read the letter. It had been left on the boarding-house counter in Chiang Mai, addressed to the landlady but sealed in an envelope from the record label that had stopped answering the duo's calls. Narong came down for coffee and saw her face. They had not played together in a week; their rehearsals had become a pair of strangers tuning in separate rooms. The letter said the label wanted only his guitar, not her voice. He took it from her, read it once, and dropped it into the stove. Neither of them spoke of it. That evening they rehearsed again, side by side, and the house cat slept on the warm lid of the rice cooker.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “a pair of strangers tuning in separate rooms” most nearly suggests that the duo's rehearsals had
options: grown louder as each musician tried to drown out the other
moved from the kitchen to a new location in the boarding house
become more efficient now that each musician practiced alone
lost the closeness and coordination the two had once shared
items.explanation: 비유 바로 앞에서 두 사람이 일주일째 함께 연주하지 않았다고 밝혀, '각자 다른 방에서 조율하는 낯선 사람들'이 단절된 상태를 뜻함을 알려 준다. 편지를 태운 뒤 그날 저녁 다시 나란히 연습했다는 대비도 그동안 잃었던 호흡이 무엇이었는지 보여 준다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A는 소리 크기, B는 실제 장소 이동, C는 효율로 비유를 잘못 읽은 것이다.

items.passage:
By noon the riverbed is a road of cracked plates,
and Clement crosses it the way he pays his debts:
slowly, one stone at a time, never looking back.
Bogdan follows with the letter in his pocket,
the apology he wrote in March and never sent,
its corners softened now to cloth.
He owes his uncle money, and something more,
a sentence he carries like a stone in a shoe,
small enough to hide, too sharp to forget.
On the far bank a goat chews a plastic bag,
and the heat makes the hills tremble.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “like a stone in a shoe” most nearly suggests that the unsent apology
options: causes Bogdan a constant, private discomfort that he cannot ignore
weighs him down so heavily that he cannot cross the dry riverbed
protects Bogdan from the sharp stones scattered across the crossing
reminds him only of the sum of money he still owes his uncle
items.explanation: 부치지 못한 사과 편지는 모서리가 천처럼 닳을 만큼 오래 주머니에 들어 있었다. 비유 바로 뒤의 '숨길 만큼 작지만 잊기엔 너무 날카롭다'는 구절은 남에게 보이지 않지만 계속 신경 쓰이는 불편함을 뜻한다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B는 무게로, C는 보호로 잘못 읽었고, D는 '그 이상의 무언가'라는 표현을 무시하고 돈만 떠올린 것이다.

items.passage: Three rules governed Angus's fish stall at the Galway market: arrive before the gulls, never haggle with a priest, and never mention the morning I stowed away on his boat. I was twelve then, hiding under a tarp because a teacher had told me I was the kind of girl who would never see past the harbor wall. Angus found me before we cleared the bay. He did not turn back. He handed me a knife and a bucket of mackerel and said that anyone aboard worked. My teacher's remark had been a locked gate; his bucket was a hinge. I have gutted fish at his stall every summer since. This morning the rain came sideways off the river, and a busker played the same three chords until noon.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “his bucket was a hinge” most nearly suggests that Angus's response
options: added a heavy new burden to the narrator's already difficult situation
opened a possibility that the teacher's remark had seemed to close off
kept the narrator confined to the boat for the rest of the voyage
reminded the narrator of the strict rules she would have to follow
items.explanation: 교사의 말은 '항구 방파제 너머를 결코 못 볼 아이'라는 단정으로, 지문은 이를 잠긴 문에 비유한다. Angus가 배를 돌리지 않고 일을 맡긴 뒤 화자가 매년 여름 그의 가판에서 일해 왔다는 점에서, 경첩은 닫힌 문을 열어 주는 계기를 뜻한다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A는 양동이를 짐으로, C는 감금으로, D는 첫 문장의 규칙으로 잘못 연결한 것이다.

items.passage: Secateurs clicked down every row of the vineyard that March in Auckland, but between Leilani and me there was only silence. She had taught me piano for six years, and when she invited me to play at her farewell concert, I said no, too quickly, and then could not explain why. For the whole harvest we worked the same slope without a word. Our silence was a vine grown across the path: each day it thickened, and each day it was harder to step over. I told myself she would speak first. She did not, and on the last afternoon I found her bucket left beside mine, half full of the grapes I had missed. I carried both to the truck. Wasps hung drowsy over the crushed fruit on the tarps.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “a vine grown across the path” most nearly suggests that the silence between Leilani and the narrator
options: was a natural part of the quiet, focused work of harvesting grapes
protected the narrator from having to explain her refusal to anyone
became a more stubborn obstacle the longer it was left alone
signaled that their friendship would only continue to grow stronger
items.explanation: 비유 바로 뒤에 '날마다 굵어지고 날마다 넘어가기 더 어려워졌다'는 설명이 붙어, 침묵이 시간이 갈수록 넘기 힘든 장애물이 되었음을 보여 준다. 화자가 상대가 먼저 말하리라 기다리기만 했다는 점도 방치된 침묵이 더 굳어졌음을 뒷받침한다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A는 수확 작업의 고요함으로, B는 보호막으로, D는 '자란다'는 말을 우정의 성장으로 잘못 읽은 것이다.

items.passage: When Amelia missed the audition for the youth orchestra, she blamed Mathis, her stepfather, who had driven her onto the wrong flyover and into an hour of Mumbai traffic. For a week she practiced in the school music room with the door shut. Mathis did not defend himself. Instead he arrived each afternoon to wait in the corridor, and on Friday he slid a notice under the door: the orchestra was holding a second round for late applicants. Amelia read it twice. Her anger did not vanish, but it ______; she opened the door and asked him to listen to her scales. Down the hall, a janitor dragged a mop bucket across the tiles.
items.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: intensified
disappeared
hardened
softened
items.explanation: Mathis가 변명 없이 매일 복도에서 기다리고 재오디션 공지를 건넨 뒤, Amelia는 문을 열고 음계를 들어 달라고 부탁한다. 다만 '분노가 사라지지는 않았다'는 앞 구절이 있으므로 완전한 소멸이 아니라 누그러짐을 뜻하는 말이 필요하다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. B는 '사라지지 않았다'와 모순되고, A와 C는 문을 여는 행동과 맞지 않는다.

items.passage: Once a week, Emre and Linh met in the quiet library on the hill, as they had for ten years, to play backgammon and review the town's accounts. Since the clinic's funding had been cut, Linh, the town's only doctor, had begun closing early, and everyone knew it. Emre, who as mayor had signed the budget, knew it best of all. Yet neither of them raised the matter. Emre asked about her garden; Linh asked about his grandson. Their conversation was ______, every topic chosen so that the true one would never surface. When the librarian dimmed the reading lamps, they set the pieces back in their box, exactly as always.
items.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: evasive
candid
heated
tedious
items.explanation: 두 사람은 진료소 예산 삭감이라는 모두가 아는 문제를 한 번도 꺼내지 않고 정원과 손자 이야기만 나눈다. 빈칸 뒤의 '진짜 화제가 떠오르지 않도록 고른 화제들'이라는 설명이 핵심을 피하는 대화임을 확인해 준다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B는 정반대 의미이고, C는 차분한 분위기와 맞지 않으며, D는 회피라는 의도를 담지 못한다.

items.passage:
Wet clay smells of rain and iron in the studio at Tromsø,
where Katarzyna, the ferryman's daughter, glazes bowls
for passengers who wait out the weather.
Anneke, who came on the morning boat, reads the word
painted on a bowl's rim and translates it aloud as farewell.
Katarzyna shakes her head. In her father's dialect
it means until the next crossing, a word that
______ a return rather than an ending.
Outside, the fjord turns slate, then silver,
and gulls ride the wind like thrown ash.
items.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: forbids
promises
regrets
conceals
items.explanation: Anneke는 그 단어를 '작별'로 옮기지만 Katarzyna는 고개를 저으며 '다음 항해까지'라는 뜻이라고 바로잡는다. 빈칸 뒤 '끝이 아니라 돌아옴'이라는 대비를 보면 그 단어는 귀환을 약속하는 말이어야 한다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A는 귀환을 막는다는 뜻이고, C는 아쉬움에 그치며, D는 뜻을 숨긴다는 의미라 문맥과 맞지 않는다.

items.passage: What do you tell a nine-year-old about land that is being sold? I asked myself this on the lakefront promenade on Chicago's South Side, where I had run into Emiliano, a farmer up from downstate, by accident. I was the surveyor who had measured his family's fields for the buyer. He was not angry, which unsettled me more than anger would have. His little brother, he said, still believed the farm would be his one day. Emiliano had decided not to lie to him but also not to frighten him; he would tell the truth in pieces small enough to carry. I found that approach more ______ than any speech I could have prepared: it was gentle without being false. Joggers passed us, and the lake slapped against the concrete steps.
items.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: deceptive
reckless
considerate
elaborate
items.explanation: Emiliano는 동생에게 거짓말하지 않되 겁을 주지도 않도록 진실을 감당할 만한 조각으로 나눠 전하기로 한다. 빈칸 뒤 '거짓 없이 다정하다'는 설명도 상대를 배려하는 태도를 가리키므로 C가 정답이다. A는 '거짓말하지 않는다'와 모순되고, B는 신중한 계획과 반대이며, D는 준비된 연설보다 낫다는 대비와 맞지 않는다.

items.passage: After the tournament in Oaxaca, where I lost to Linton in eleven moves in front of the whole club, I avoided him for a month. I had played Gyeongho's favorite opening, the one he had taught me, and I had played it badly. Then one evening Linton and I ended up on the same station platform, waiting for a delayed train. I expected him to gloat. Instead he took out a pocket set and showed me where my seventh move had gone wrong, patiently, the way someone might help a friend tie a knot. His manner was so ______ that my embarrassment began to seem less like a wound than a lesson. The train arrived, and a vendor packed away the last of her tamales.
items.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: triumphant
dismissive
impatient
unassuming
items.explanation: 화자는 Linton이 우쭐댈 것이라 예상했지만, 그는 친구의 매듭을 묶어 주듯 차분하게 실수를 짚어 준다. 그 결과 창피함이 상처가 아니라 교훈처럼 느껴졌다는 점에서 겸손하고 거들먹거리지 않는 태도를 뜻하는 말이 필요하다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A는 화자가 예상했지만 일어나지 않은 태도이고, B와 C는 '참을성 있게'라는 묘사와 모순된다.

items.passage: We had argued for weeks about the table. I wanted the terrace laid the Galician way for my mother's visit, with octopus on wooden plates and bread torn by hand; Genevieve insisted on the long French lunch her grandmother used to serve, course after careful course. Both of us worked nights at the hospital, and we fought the way tired people fight, in clipped sentences over cold coffee. I kept a list of every dish she rejected. Then, on the morning itself, I watched her mother teaching mine to fold a crêpe, the two of them laughing at the mess, and the list in my pocket seemed suddenly small and a little foolish. We set out both kinds of plates. Below the terrace, the vines dripped from the night's rain.
items.question: Which choice best describes the shift in tone in the text?
options: From cheerful anticipation to anxious dread about the mothers' first meeting
From calm detachment to bitter resentment over Genevieve's many demands
From playful teasing to solemn regret about the weeks spent arguing
From weary irritation to rueful amusement at the narrator's own pettiness
items.explanation: 앞부분은 피곤한 사람들이 짧은 말로 다투고 화자가 거절된 요리 목록까지 적어 두는 짜증스러운 어조다. 두 어머니가 크레이프를 접으며 웃는 모습을 본 뒤 화자는 주머니 속 목록이 '작고 조금 어리석게' 느껴졌다고 말하며 자신을 가볍게 비웃는다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A와 B는 변화 방향이 반대이고, C의 '장난스러운 놀림'은 앞부분과 맞지 않는다.

items.passage: Rain beaded on the manuscript pages Jiayi had carried to the stone bridge, and she shielded them with her sleeve while Haoran read. He had translated four of her novels and praised every ending. Tonight he praised the river, the lanterns, the noodle shop behind them, everything except the final chapter. Jiayi laughed and teased him for turning into a poet. Then he handed the pages back without a word about them, and she understood. The ending she had rewritten six times was still wrong, and he had been too kind, for too long, to say so. She stood very still while the traffic hissed over the wet stones. A boy on a scooter honked twice at nobody.
items.question: Which choice best describes the shift in tone in the text?
options: From lighthearted banter to a sober recognition of an unwelcome truth
From tense suspicion to warm relief once Haoran praises the manuscript
From quiet sadness to growing excitement about rewriting the ending
From formal politeness to open anger at Haoran's dishonest flattery
items.explanation: 앞부분에서 Jiayi는 Haoran이 강과 등불만 칭찬하자 시인이 되었다며 웃으며 놀린다. 그러나 그가 원고에 대해 한마디도 없이 돌려주자 결말이 여전히 잘못되었다는 사실을 깨닫고 꼼짝 않고 서 있게 된다. 가벼운 농담에서 받아들이기 싫은 진실을 인정하는 진지함으로 바뀌므로 A가 정답이다. B와 C는 변화 방향이 반대이고, D의 분노는 지문에 드러나지 않는다.
